title: Bridge Conductor Playbook and Staffing Micro‑Sprints
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the Bridge Conductor role, a lightweight staffing and orchestration pattern we use for fast multi‑team incident response. It formalizes 30–90 minute "micro‑sprints" for focused restoration work, telemetry triage lanes, and a CSR liaison thread for customer messaging. The goal is faster containment, clearer cross‑team accountability, and repeatable status cadence.

Scope

- Applies to production incidents affecting Redwood API, Dedicated, or Private deployment control planes and serving runtime where more than one engineering team must coordinate.
- NOT intended for single‑service incidents resolved by an oncall owner in under 15 minutes (use the standard runbook).

When to invoke a Bridge Conductor

1. Incident escalates past page severity P1/P2 and requires cross‑functional triage (serving runtime + networking + infra).
2. Multiple services show correlated SLO degradation or increased 5xx rate across regions.
3. Customer‑impacting regressions where proactive CSR messaging is required.

Bridge Conductor role (BC) — responsibilities

- Single point of orchestration for the duration of the bridge.
- Maintain and publish the status cadence every micro‑sprint boundary.
- Assign micro‑sprint objectives and accept completion signoff.
- Coordinate CSR liaison updates and ensure they are approved.
- Authorize model or capacity rollbacks per rollback authorization matrix.
- Track action items to completion; if unresolved after 3 micro‑sprints, escalate to Incident Commander.

Staffing model and micro‑sprints

- Micro‑sprint length: default 30 minutes (can extend to 60 or 90 based on scope).
- Roles per bridge: Bridge Conductor, Micro‑sprint Leads (one per focus lane), Oncall Engineers (per service), CSR Liaison, SRE Support (capacity/infra).
- Suggested staffing for a 30‑minute micro‑sprint: 1 BC, 3 Micro‑sprint Leads, 6 engineers, 1 CSR Liaison, 1 SRE Support.

Micro‑sprint lifecycle (30‑minute example)

1. Start (0:00) — BC opens bridge, publishes initial status (see "Status templates"), declares lanes, and assigns leads.
2. Diagnosis (0:00–0:10) — Leads collect evidence in parallel: latency histograms, kv cache hit/miss, GPU queue length, instance health.
3. Action (0:10–0:25) — Leads implement a single focused mitigation (e.g., eviction of large prefixes, throttle policy change, scale pool +1).
4. Verify & signoff (0:25–0:30) — Leads confirm metrics trend, announce results in bridge, BC publishes updated status and next steps.
5. Close or continue — If resolved, BC closes bridge and initiates postmortem intake. If not, next micro‑sprint begins with updated objectives.

Telemetry triage lanes

Create parallel lanes to speed evidence collection. Each lane has a named lead and checklist. Example lanes:

- Serving Runtime Lane (Lead: runtime engineer)
  - Metrics: per‑model 95th/99th token latency, KV cache hit rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
  - Quick checks: kernel error logs, OOM traces, quantization fallback count.

- Ingress & Networking Lane (Lead: infra engineer)
  - Metrics: LB error rates, TLS handshake failure, NAT gateway saturation, region‑to‑region mesh latency.
  - Quick checks: BGP/route flaps, firewall rules change, certificate expiration.

- Capacity & Autoscale Lane (Lead: SRE)
  - Metrics: node count, queue length per shard, pod crashloop, GPU memory pressure.
  - Quick checks: recent deploys, autoscaler logs, throttling events.

- Billing/Quota & Customer Impact (Lead: CSR Liaison)
  - Metrics: per‑tenant 429/403 spikes, quota enforcements, billing alerts.
  - Quick checks: tenant‑level logs, usage spikes, tenant config changes.

Runbook bootstrap checklist (BC)

1. Confirm incident classification and severity.
2. Create/attach central evidence doc (link in bridge).
3. Declare lanes and assign leads.
4. Publish initial status message with impact, ETA, what we are doing.
5. Confirm CSR liaison and legal contact if customer‑sensitive.

Decision matrix and rollback authorization

- Minor config change (non‑customer visible) — Micro‑sprint Lead approval.
- Autoscale / capacity tweak — SRE approval + BC endorsement.
- Model rollback or heavy config rollback — Incident Commander approval.

Status page & customer comms templates

Use the following status cadence: Initial (within 10 min), Sprint boundary updates (every 30 min), Resolution (at close), Postmortem notice (24–48 hrs).

Initial status template (10 min)

- Title: [INVESTIGATING] Elevated inference latency in us‑west
- Impact: Some API requests for text generation are taking >2s (seen by ~12% of requests).
- Scope: A subset of hosted model endpoints in us‑west and one Dedicated cluster.
- What we are doing: Running parallel lanes (runtime, infra, capacity) and performing targeted rollbacks where safe.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.

Sprint update template (30 min cadence)

- Title: [UPDATE] Inference latency: verification of mitigation
- What changed: Increased pool size +1 in us‑west; KV cache eviction executed for 3 large prefixes.
- Effect: 95th percentile latency reduced from 2.4s to 1.1s for the affected endpoints.
- Next steps: Continue monitoring; prepare for controlled rollback of recent model patch if metrics regress.

Customer CSR terse template (for tenant‑facing support)

- Subject: Incident affecting inference latency (our reference INV‑2026‑074)
- Body: We experienced elevated latency impacting some requests between 10:05–11:40 UTC. Our engineering team applied mitigation and latency has returned to normal. We will follow up with a fuller incident summary and corrective actions in 24–48 hours.

Postmortem intake & quality gates

- Postmortem owner: BC or Incident Commander (if escalated).
- Intake timeline: Draft within 48 hours; peer review within 96 hours.
- Required sections: impact timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence artifacts (metrics + logs), mitigation steps taken, long‑term fix, action owners, and verification plan.

Game day design (focus areas)

- Run a quarterly "Bridge Conductor" game day that simulates a correlated KV cache + autoscaler bug affecting 2 regions.
- Exercises should validate: micro‑sprint cadence, lane parallelism, CSR liaison approval flow, rollback matrix, and postmortem intake.
- Scoring rubric: time to first meaningful mitigation (goal <15 min), time to verified recovery (goal <90 min), quality of customer messaging.

Operational tooling and templates (cheat sheet)

- Bridge creation (CLI): rwd bridge create --title "INV: high latency us‑west" --severity P1 --lane runtime,ingress,capacity --owner @aisha
- Evidence doc template header (copy into bridge):
  - Incident start: YYYY‑MM‑DD hh:mm UTC
  - Services impacted: list
  - Attach: grafana links, logs link, trace ids

Appendix: quick checklists

- Ten‑minute triage checklist:
  1. Confirm alerts and scope.
  2. Verify deploys in last 60 minutes.
  3. Take safe rollback snapshot (if applicable).
  4. Notify CSR + Legal for customer‑facing incidents.

- Bridge closure checklist:
  1. Verify SLOs back to baseline for at least one micro‑sprint period.
  2. Close bridge and mark evidence doc with final timeline.
  3. Open postmortem intake and assign owner.
  4. Publish customer postmortem if tenant‑impacting and required by SLA.
